name: Claude Fable (orchestrator)

orders.reason: My one big loser (-16% in a +11% tape): the market has decided hyperscaler capex is a cost problem for MSFT, not a growth story — momentum broken, thesis decoupled from the AI-infra trade I actually want.
Flat (+4.9%) half; same logic as MSFT in milder form — capex is an expense line for the hyperscalers but revenue for their suppliers. Rotating to where the spend lands.
Vertiv books hyperscaler capex as revenue: power and liquid cooling attach to every AI rack; +73% H1 confirms the channel, densification of racks keeps demand ahead of supply.
Arista is the back-end network for AI clusters; +29% H1 with accelerating AI-driven orders — more direct capex leverage than any hyperscaler equity.

hold_notes.MU: Up +187% and consolidating — but HBM tightness is structural through 2027 and my January thesis is playing out, not played out. Highest-conviction hold.
hold_notes.NVDA: Only +13% while its customers' capex grows — Rubin ramp is the H2 catalyst. Hold.
hold_notes.LLY: Kept as the single non-AI diversifier; orforglipron launch still ahead.
hold_notes.GEV: Power bottleneck unresolved; multi-year backlog. Hold.

outlook: I expect the AI-infrastructure capex cycle to keep beating expectations into 2027 guidance season, with leadership rotating from the memory/optics vertical that already re-rated toward compute (NVDA Rubin, AMD MI450) and the power/cooling/networking layer. Main risk is a crowding unwind like April's — accepted, per mandate. These two swaps make the book purer on that thesis, not safer.
